project.name: mruby
project.commit_note: Stage 01 reproduced against the preserved vulnerable checkout under `gt_results/secbench_oss_mruby.ossfuzz-42538578/_work/src`, whose `HEAD` matches the metadata vulnerable commit.

staged_source_snapshot.description: This staged vulnerable checkout matches the saved ASan line map: `mrb_load_detect_file_cxt()` is at `parse.y:6962`, `cipush()` reallocates at `src/vm.c:349`, and the crashing stale-register read is at `src/vm.c:2672`.

classification.classification_note: The saved crash is an AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free read in `mrb_vm_exec`. A nested Ruby call made from `mrb_ary_splat()` grows and reallocates the VM callinfo array in `cipush()`, but the outer interpreter loop keeps using its stale `ci` pointer and then expands `regs` through freed `mrb_callinfo` storage when it fetches `ci->stack`.

bug_description.original: Heap-use-after-free in the mruby VM (mrb_vm_exec in src/vm.c). During certain VM execution paths (involving cipush/mrb_ary_splat and nested mrb_vm_exec calls) an object is reallocated/freed (mrb_realloc/mrb_realloc_simple) while still referenced by the VM, and the VM later reads from that freed heap memory. This can cause crashes and undefined behavior, and may enable memory corruption or further exploitation with crafted inputs.
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free READ of size 8` at `src/vm.c:2672` while the staged vulnerable `mruby` CLI executed the exact saved 7597-byte Ruby witness. `mrb_load_detect_file_cxt()` reads the witness as plain Ruby source and routes it into `mrb_load_exec()`. On the crashing path, the outer `mrb_vm_exec()` loop snapshots `mrb_callinfo *ci = mrb->c->ci`, and `regs` is the macro alias `ci->stack`. Later `OP_ARYCAT` calls `mrb_ary_splat(mrb, regs[a+1])`. Because the operand is not already an Array but does respond to `to_a`, `mrb_ary_splat()` reenters Ruby through `mrb_funcall_argv()`. That nested send reaches `cipush()`, where the exhausted callinfo stack takes the `mrb_realloc()` branch and frees or moves the old `mrb->c->cibase`; the saved ASan free stack points exactly to `src/vm.c:349`, and the reported address lies inside that freed 1536-byte callinfo array. Vulnerable `OP_ARYCAT` then resumes without the `ci = mrb->c->ci;` refresh added by the patch, so the next `regs[a]` access at line 2672 first dereferences stale outer `ci` to fetch `ci->stack` from freed `mrb_callinfo` memory and triggers the saved UAF read.

source.description: First project-side read of the attacker-controlled PoC file into mruby's source-loader buffer.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` has sha256 `b1df4af00e33920a47af3f03b900f141c94b930de9fca6de39833e6878c7b2d7` and length 7597 bytes. This statement materializes its first `DETECT_SIZE` bytes into `leading.b` and sets the `bufsize` later used by the source-versus-bytecode admission check.

sink.description: Crash sink. After `cipush()` reallocates and frees the old callinfo array, this branch still expands `regs` through the stale outer `ci`, so `ci->stack` is fetched from freed `mrb_callinfo` memory before `regs[a]` is tested.
sink.note: The saved ASan report shows `READ of size 8` at `src/vm.c:2672:11` on address `0x51b000000668`, 1512 bytes inside the freed 1536-byte region `[0x51b000000080,0x51b000000680)`.

root_cause.description: Root cause fixed by the patch. This helper call can reenter Ruby and let `cipush()` reallocate `mrb->c->cibase`, but vulnerable `OP_ARYCAT` falls through to later `regs[...]` uses without refreshing `ci = mrb->c->ci;`; the patch adds that missing refresh immediately after this call.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-controlled Ruby witness enters project code here. Its bytes drive source admission, compilation, and the later `OP_ARYCAT`/`mrb_ary_splat` execution path that reaches the stale-register UAF.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific format gate. The saved witness is admitted as plain Ruby source rather than a `RITE` bytecode image, enabling the parser and VM path that reaches `OP_ARYCAT`.

admitted_location.code: return mrb_load_exec(mrb, mrb_parse_file_continue(mrb, fp, leading.b, bufsize, c), c);

evidence_limitations: Stage 02 stayed source-grounded and did not rerun or instrument the fixed build. `patch_resolves` below is therefore based on the staged diff's direct repair of the missing `ci = mrb->c->ci;` refresh, not on fixed-version dynamic validation.

The exact high-level Ruby construct inside the malformed 7597-byte witness that compiles to the crashing `OP_ARYCAT` / `to_a` path is not statically recoverable from the saved artifacts alone. The trace below therefore anchors at source admission and then follows the exact C-level path proven by the staged source and saved ASan call stacks.

coarse_trace.summary: The CLI reproduction reads the exact saved witness and admits it as Ruby source, so mruby parses and executes the script instead of taking the `RITE` bytecode loader path.
The outer interpreter loop snapshots its current `ci` and therefore its `regs` base, then reaches `OP_ARYCAT`, which forwards `regs[a+1]` into `mrb_ary_splat()`.
Because the operand responds to `to_a`, `mrb_ary_splat()` reenters Ruby through `mrb_funcall_argv()`, and the nested send reaches `cipush()`, which reallocates and frees the old callinfo array.

The outer `OP_ARYCAT` resumes without refreshing `ci`, so the next `regs[a]` test still dereferences stale outer `ci` and fetches `ci->stack` from freed callinfo storage, producing the saved UAF read.

fine_trace.note: Source. The staged CLI reproduction opens the saved `poc` file and reads attacker-controlled bytes into `leading.b`. This is the first project statement that materializes input data on the crashing path.
The witness is admitted as Ruby source, not a `RITE` binary, so execution continues through parsing and bytecode execution instead of the binary loader path.

depends_on.via: bufsize < sizeof(leading.h) || memcmp(leading.h.binary_ident, RITE_BINARY_IDENT, sizeof(leading.h.binary_ident)) != 0 || memchr(leading.b, '\0', bufsize) == NULL

fine_trace.note: The outer interpreter loop snapshots the current callinfo into local `ci`; in this function `regs` is the macro alias `ci->stack`, so later register accesses are tied to this specific callinfo block until `ci` is refreshed.

depends_on.via: mrb_load_exec(mrb, mrb_parse_file_continue(mrb, fp, leading.b, bufsize, c), c)

fine_trace.note: On the crashing path the parsed script reaches `OP_ARYCAT`, which passes the current register operand `regs[a+1]` into `mrb_ary_splat()` while the outer frame still relies on the local aliases from step 3. The saved ASan free stack identifies this exact call site.

fine_trace.code: mrb_value ary = mrb_funcall_argv(mrb, v, MRB_SYM(to_a), 0, NULL);
fine_trace.note: The operand is not handled by the earlier fast paths, so `mrb_ary_splat()` reenters Ruby by calling `to_a` on `v` instead of merely duplicating an existing Array or wrapping the value. This nested Ruby call is the reentry that can change VM callinfo storage.

fine_trace.code: ci = cipush(mrb, n, CINFO_DIRECT, NULL, NULL, BLK_PTR(blk), 0, 0);
fine_trace.note: The reentrant `to_a` send enters `mrb_funcall_with_block()`, whose direct `cipush()` call pushes a new VM call frame for the nested Ruby dispatch. This is the exact caller proven by the saved ASan free stack immediately above `cipush()`.

Because the current callinfo stack is full on the witnessed path, `cipush()` takes the reallocation branch, and `mrb_realloc()` frees or moves the old `c->cibase` region. The saved ASan free context points exactly to this statement, so any outer aliases into the old callinfo array become dangling after this step.

Root cause. After `mrb_ary_splat()` returns, vulnerable `OP_ARYCAT` does not refresh `ci = mrb->c->ci;`, so the outer frame keeps using the stale `ci` from step 3. Because `regs` is `ci->stack`, the next register access will fetch `ci->stack` from the freed pre-realloc `mrb_callinfo` array. The patch adds that refresh immediately after this call.

Sink. Evaluating the branch expands `regs` as `ci->stack`, so the stale outer `ci` is dereferenced after step 7 to load `ci->stack` from the freed 1536-byte `mrb_callinfo` region, producing the saved 8-byte heap-use-after-free read.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch is source-consistent with the root cause because it refreshes `ci = mrb->c->ci;` immediately after `mrb_ary_splat()` and similar reentrant helpers, but Stage 02 did not execute the fixed build and therefore does not claim dynamic confirmation.

format.name: Plain mruby source file
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact staged 7597-byte witness at `gt_results/secbench_oss_mruby.ossfuzz-42538578/poc` (sha256 `b1df4af00e33920a47af3f03b900f141c94b930de9fca6de39833e6878c7b2d7`). Source and saved ASan evidence show only this narrow contract: the file must remain plain-text Ruby admitted by `mrb_load_detect_file_cxt()`, and on the vulnerable build its execution must reach `OP_ARYCAT`, invoke `mrb_ary_splat()` on a value that reenters Ruby via `to_a`, drive `cipush()` through the callinfo reallocation branch, and then return to outer `OP_ARYCAT` without refreshing `ci` before the `regs[a]` read at `src/vm.c:2672`. No broader input class is claimed here.
